newsitem.title: USA: HORSE RACING-DERBY FAVORITES IN MIDDLE FOR RACE.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-DERBY FAVORITES IN MIDDLE FOR RACE.

text.p: The favourites for Saturday's 123rd running of the Kentucky Derby drew post positions on Wednesday close together in the middle of the smallest field since 1985 to contest the American classic.

Pulpit, which blazed through a five-furlong workout on Monday in 1:00 and 2/5 of a second, and has won four times in five starts this year, was established as the 2-1 favourite, breaking out of the No. 7 spot.

Inside of the favourite in the No. 4 spot was Captain Bodgit, the only horse to beat Pulpit this year and the second favourite at 5-2. Third favoured Silver Charm, who has never finished worse than second in a six-race career, was in the No. 5 post position at 5-1.
The $1 million race for 3-year-olds will be contested over the famed Churchill Downs track at 1-1/4 miles with a 13-horse field, the smallest since Spend a Buck won a wire-to-wire victory in 1985.
"I was hoping for number four to eight," said Pulpit's trainer, Frank Brothers, "so the draw was wonderful for my horse. The small field is a big plus for everybody."

Pulpit, who will be ridden by Shane Sellers, is trying to become the first Derby favourite to win since Spectaclar Bid in 1979 and the first horse to win a Derby who did not race as a 2-year-old since Appolo in 1882.
Captain Bodgit's trainer, Gary Capuano, was also pleased with his spot, saying he didn't care where the horse broke from as long he avoided the extreme inside or the outside.

"He's been running great here," Capuano said of the second favourite, who will be ridden by Alex Solis and won is coming off wins in the Wood Memorial at New York's Aqueduct track and the Florida Derby at Gulfstream Park, where he beat Pulpit by 2-1/2 lengths.

Silver Charm, with Gary Stevens aboard, is the California challenger who won the San Vincente at Santa Anita but finished second to Free House, the 8-1, fourth favourite, in his last two races, the San Felipe and the Santa Anita Derby.
Bob Baffert, trainer of Silver Charm, said he was relieved that the horse did not draw the No. 1 post position, saying "I wanted to be in the middle."
That No. 1 spot went to Crypto Star, a 10-1 longshot that likes to run from off the pace.

The longest shot in the race was the 50-1 Deeds Not Words, trained by D. Wayne Lukas, the winner of Derby in 1995 and 1996. He said the odds were "probably pretty accurate" for the horse, which has run four times and never finished better than third.
